Article 34

The rule was printed in the code of ethics

On the sixth of June, 1924, the National Association of Real Estate Boards adopted Article 34 of its Code of Ethics. A realtor, it said, should never be instrumental in introducing into a neighborhood members of any race whose presence will clearly be detrimental to property values.

This was enforceable. Every member board had to adopt the code, agents could be disciplined, and boards that refused could be expelled.

Chicago had got there first. Its own board voted in 1921 to expel any member who sold to a Black buyer on a white block.

26
years the rule stood in the national code, from 1924 until the racial language was removed in 1950
